analogies: A prompt is like a brief to a freelancer: the clearer the brief, the less rework.
definition: A prompt is everything you send the model to get a response: your question, any instructions about tone or format, and background material it should use. The model reads the whole prompt, then predicts the most likely good continuation. Change the prompt and you change the answer, sometimes dramatically — which is why two people asking the 'same' thing can get very different results.

edges.label: you write this one
edges.note: Your prompt is what you type; the system prompt is the hidden instruction set from whoever built the app.

edges.label: made of tokens
edges.note: Every word of your prompt is tokenized and billed as input tokens.

edges.label: fills the window
edges.note: Long prompts eat into the same context window the answer needs.

example.body: You type 'write about our launch' and get generic marketing fluff. You try again: 'Write a 3-sentence announcement for our launch on June 4, aimed at existing customers, friendly tone, mention the 20% early-bird discount.' Same AI, same afternoon — completely different result. The second prompt did the work: audience, length, tone, and the one fact the model couldn't have known.
example.title: The vague request vs the specific one

footnotes.body: Prompts are tokenized and placed at the start of the context window; system prompts typically carry more weight in instruction-tuned models. Prompt engineering shades into harness design when prompts are assembled programmatically with tool definitions and retrieved context.
footnotes.label: For the technical reader

name: Prompt
tagline: The instructions and context you give the AI before it answers — the words that shape what comes back.
whyItMatters: The prompt is the one part of the AI you fully control. Small changes — adding an example, stating the audience, pasting in the relevant document — are often the difference between a useless answer and exactly what you needed, and they cost nothing to try.
